# Bay Area wedding venue comparison
Status: source collection started with two initial operator records; coverage incomplete and charts pending.

## Coverage
Working proposal: nine Bay Area counties; adjacent destination competitors separately tagged. Geographic boundary not yet agreed. Deduplicate by operator/property while keeping distinct spaces/packages. Track official URL, discovery source, active/closed/unconfirmed status, checked dates and gaps. No exhaustive inventory claimed.

## Comparison fields
- Capacity: seated dinner plus dance floor vs standing; indoor and weather-backup capacity.
- Prices: venue-only vs package, headcount/day/season/duration/year, minimum spend, ceremony fee, extra hours, all mandatory taxes/service/rental/staff/security/cleanup charges, deposits/refunds/cancellation.
- Inclusions: venue, chairs/tables, basic rentals, decor, setup/reset, kitchen/prep space, getting-ready rooms, exclusivity.
- Outside vendors: approved lists, fees/restrictions, catering and alcohol/BYOB/bartender rules.
- Hours: separate indoor/outdoor amplified music, alcohol service, guest departure and cleanup. Midnight status needs evidence.
- Travel: parking/shuttle, nearby hotels, airports/cities, date/time-dependent road journeys; lodging room/capacity/exclusivity.
- Other: restrooms, accessibility, rain/heat/smoke backup, power/lighting/storage/load-in, decoration/fire rules, insurance, permitted annual events and public availability.

## Normalization and economics
Compare full mandatory customer cost at stated headcount/date/duration; show food/drink inclusions. Refundable deposits are cash requirements, not automatically expenses. Label quote-only, starting-at, verified published values and modeled values separately.

Price does not reveal profit. Low/base/high scenarios need realized booking revenue, bookings/seasonality, per-event labor/cleanup/security/rentals, fixed rent/utilities/insurance/marketing/maintenance, owner pay, startup capital and booking-ramp cash reserves.

## Planned charts
Comparable mandatory price vs capacity; hours/vendor flexibility; geography/travel; break-even bookings/seasonality. No numerical charts until enough comparable sourced observations exist.
## Research scope clarification — 2026-10-11T03:38:07Z
- Calculate realistic capital requirements from the evidence; do not impose an upfront budget ceiling or repeat the budget-cap question.
- Compare four routes without selecting one: lease an existing lawful venue; convert leased space; buy land and develop; buy an established venue.
- Desired ability to host 300–400 guests. Whether this is normal or peak capacity remains unknown; no minimum/approved occupancy established.
- Prefer open/separated space to reduce noise issues, but acreage does not establish permitted event use, midnight hours or sound compliance.
- Research comprehensive relevant data with source dates, confidence, explicit gaps and low/base/high scenarios. No exhaustive coverage or actual competitor profits claimed.
Record marketing capacity, actual permitted occupancy, seated dinner/dance-floor capacity and weather-backup capacity separately. Add usable event area/acreage, neighboring residences, sound conditions, approved annual events, parking/overflow/shuttle, deal type, asking price/date and real estate inclusion. Seller profitability claims need verification.
## Initial operator observations
- [Deer Park Villa FAQ](https://deerparkvilla.com/faq/) and [packages](https://deerparkvilla.com/packages/): Fairfax/Marin; published capacity 200 indoors and 300 outdoors, layout confirmation required. Preferred vendors are mentioned; unrestricted vendor choice is not established. Midnight permission and total mandatory price unknown.

Capacity, end time, venue-only availability and full price unknown on this reviewed page. Bundled offering must be normalized before comparison.

# Property and operating feasibility
Early screening questions; no property-specific clearance or commitment.

## Verified starting source
[Solano County special-event facilities](https://www.solanocounty.gov/government/resource-management/planning-services/development-programs/special-event-facilities), checked 2026-10-11T03:33:01Z. Official page describes zoning/size/frequency requirements, permit steps, example fees and involvement of planning, building, environmental health and public works. Applies to unincorporated Solano, not automatically all Bay Area cities/counties. Linked detailed guide not yet reviewed.

## Questions to investigate before commitment
Permitted recurring paid event use at exact parcel/building; transferability of existing permits; capacity, event count, noise, operating hours and alcohol approvals; landlord consent and obligations if approvals fail; assembly occupancy, fire access/exits, accessible facilities, bathrooms, parking/transport, utilities/septic/water, neighbor impacts and weather/emergency backup.

Test venue-only operations: setup/reset, security, cleaning, safety, vendor coordination, rental maintenance, sales/tours and incident response still need assigned responsibility. Customer-hired vendors do not establish owner workload.

Compare all mandatory customer costs with rent, event contribution, operator pay, improvements and cash reserves. Validate actual target-couple interest. Compare land development, existing lawful venue lease and management/revenue-share options after clarifying constraints.

## Hypotheses
Leasing may reduce some development uncertainty, but lease obligations/improvements may still be costly. Creative decor can add labor/storage/reset costs. Land asking price is only part of usable-site cost. Midnight must distinguish music, alcohol, guest departure and cleanup. No cost/profit or permit outcome established.

- Calculate realistic capital requirements from the evidence; do not impose an upfront budget ceiling or repeat the budget-cap question.
- Compare four routes without selecting one: lease an existing lawful venue; convert leased space; buy land and develop; buy an established venue.
- Desired ability to host 300–400 guests. Whether this is normal or peak capacity remains unknown; no minimum/approved occupancy established.

- Research comprehensive relevant data with source dates, confidence, explicit gaps and low/base/high scenarios. No exhaustive coverage or actual competitor profits claimed.
Acquisition diligence: business-only leasehold vs business plus real estate; verify financials and owner labor, booking/customer-deposit obligations, deferred maintenance, permit/license/lease transfer, title and contracts. wiki.Four business routes:
# Four-route capital and operations model
Status: framework; sourced dollar estimates not yet collected. Updated UTC: 2026-10-11T03:38:07Z.

| Route | Capital to quantify | Key evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lease lawful venue | Deposit, ramp-up rent, repairs/design, equipment, approvals, professional fees and reserves | Lease terms, permitted use/capacity/hours, quotes |
| Convert leased space | Above plus design, approvals, construction, fire/accessibility/occupancy, utilities, bathrooms, parking | Building/parcel records, approval conditions, scope-specific quotes, lease allocation |
| Buy land and develop | Land/closing, investigations, design/permits, access, utilities/septic, parking, structures, finance carrying costs and reserves | Actual parcels, infrastructure feasibility, approvals, quotes and schedule |
| Buy established venue | Business and/or real estate price, closing/diligence, equipment, repairs, booking liabilities, financing and reserves | Verified financial history, deal structure, permits, contracts/lease and title |

Model 300 and 400 seated guests with dining/dancing and lawful facilities; do not assume land area implies approved capacity. Keep smaller competitors as benchmarks without replacing the desired flexibility.

## Outputs
Total project cost; required cash/equity vs debt; pre-opening carry/time; fixed monthly cost; variable event/headcount cost; contribution; break-even bookings; owner/manager compensation; debt service; booking ramp/seasonality; peak cash deficit and contingency. Capital need is an output, not a predefined ceiling.

Separate operating profit, cash flow and debt repayment. Customer deposits may carry performance/refund liabilities. No confidential competitor profits asserted.

## Every observation
Value/unit, property/route/headcount/date/duration, original source URL/document, quote/publication/check dates, exclusions/taxes, status (verified, asking price, seller claim, assumption, unknown), confidence and sensitivity. Use ranges when one figure is unsupported.

## Acquisition diligence
Business-only/leasehold vs business plus real estate, valuation allocation, actual bookings/revenue/margins, owner labor/add-backs, deposits/unfulfilled events, liabilities/contracts/staff, deferred maintenance, transferable approvals/licenses, lease assignment/title/easements, permitted event count/hours/capacity and reason for sale. Asking price is not valuation.

Initial source: [SBA planning and buying-business guidance](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/plan-your-business/), checked 2026-10-11T03:38:07Z. General guidance, not actual transaction documents or financing quotes.

# What a planner needs from every venue

Original Bay Leaf synthesis • 194 research fields in 18 categories • reviewed October 10, 2026 (Pacific).

Start with suitability, then investigate logistics and complete cost. Every venue gets the same framework; irrelevant fields become **Not applicable** with a reason. Unknown never means allowed, included, free or zero. This is a proposed research standard, not verified answers for all venues.

## The answer format

For each field record: **answer • evidence/status • source URL or written document • date checked • package/date/guest-count assumptions • unresolved question • person responsible • next action/deadline**. Keep quotes and private correspondence in shared private context, not the public website.

Evidence labels: **Authority/document verified; Operator published; Directory reported; Observed on visit; Assumption/calculated; Unknown — inquire; Conflicting; Not applicable; Prohibited/closed**. Written sales answers do not establish legal occupancy. A permission can have conditions; preserve them.

## Research stages

1. Broad inventory: capture leads even when wedding permission is unknown. Do not silently discard unconventional spaces.
2. Uniform inquiry: request terms and itemized prices before tours. Use guest-count scenarios for research without pretending they are booked plans.
3. Joint visit: walk the guest route, supplier route and weather backup with floor plans; check equipment and responsibility gaps.
4. Contract validation: reconcile every promised inclusion and exception with the final terms and relevant approvals.
5. Business review: separately examine repeat use, improvements, operating effort and financial feasibility.

The public comparison should show the useful summary. Expandable details hold the full checklist rather than forcing every question into a very wide table. Filter by status, county, venue type, capacity basis, price basis and restrictions; sort unknowns last.

[California ABC caterer permits](https://www.abc.ca.gov/licensing/license-forms/caterers-permit/) · [San Francisco entertainment permit guidance](https://www.sf.gov/get-place-entertainment-permit-your-business) · [Sonoma proposed special-event zoning update](https://sonoma-county.legistar.com/LegislationDetail.aspx?GUID=3795E6F1-7701-4414-AB81-C8BB81143BC1&ID=7768001) · [Ready.gov business emergency plans](https://www.ready.gov/business/emergency-plans)

- Recurring commercial-use approval
- Event-frequency restrictions
- Lawful music hours/conditions
- Lease/sublease event rights
- Permit/license transfer conditions
- Septic/water/electrical capacity
- Fire-access and occupancy upgrade costs
- Staffing hours per event
- Maintenance/storage/security costs
- Capital cost and lead-time scenarios
- Contribution per event
- Break-even events and working capital
- Acquisition financial verification
- Government rental versus concession rights

## Cost per head: compare the same thing

Maintain three distinct measures: **venue-only ÷ guests**, **food/bar package per guest**, and **required event total ÷ guests**. The last is the useful comparison only when all mandatory components are known. It does not include optional photographer, attire or other whole-wedding spending unless explicitly selected.

For a comparable scenario, calculate the applicable venue/space fee + contracted food/bar spend after its minimum + mandatory staffing/rentals + compulsory access, cleaning, transport and permit costs + service charges and tax on their documented bases. Divide by the stated guest count. Count included items once. Keep refundable deposits as cash needed, not an event expense. Avoid adding a package rate to a minimum if the minimum already covers that package.

Record children/vendor-meal treatment and date/season. A “from” price has no known upper bound. If required charges are missing, show a **partial known subtotal**, not an all-in range. Do not manufacture a maximum from an optimistic estimate. Capital required for the business remains a research output, not an imposed budget limit.

## What is especially easy to miss

- A wet-weather room may exist yet be unreserved or too small for dinner plus dancing.
- An item can be available on site without being included; quantities and setup labor matter.
- Vendor lists can be optional, mandatory, or subject to an exception fee.
- A five-hour reception does not identify music cutoff, bar closure, or final departure.
- A high maximum may describe standing use, not the intended seating/dancing layout.
- “Hands-off ownership” still requires named responsibility for safety, guest issues, load-in, cleaning and lockup. Model paid labor and owner hours separately.

## California and Bay Area checks

California ABC states that Type 58 catered alcohol events require event authorization and ordinarily have a 36-event annual limit at a location, with an exception process. This is not a general cap on weddings and does not determine every BYOB arrangement. Treat the alcohol operating route and any exception as a business due-diligence question. [ABC official FAQ](https://www.abc.ca.gov/licensing/license-forms/caterers-permit/).

Accessibility is a continuous experience through arrival, rooms, seating and restrooms. “Historic” or “grandfathered” is not an automatic ADA exemption. [DOJ small-business guidance](https://www.ada.gov/resources/title-iii-primer/).

Do not convert a one-time special-event rental into assumed permission for weekly commercial weddings. Confirm actual jurisdiction, land-use entitlement, permit conditions, occupancy, fire access, noise and food/wastewater requirements for the property. The reviewed Sonoma staff report contains proposed changes, not proof of final adoption; numerical thresholds remain unverified. [Sonoma source](https://sonoma-county.legistar.com/LegislationDetail.aspx?GUID=3795E6F1-7701-4414-AB81-C8BB81143BC1&ID=7768001).

## Source review and limitations

- [A Practical Wedding planning workbooks](https://apracticalwedding.com/planner/) — Public resource descriptions reviewed; embedded workbook links not extracted.
- [Here Comes the Guide venue questions and worksheet](https://www.herecomestheguide.com/wedding-ideas/questions-to-ask-your-wedding-venue) — Article and eight-page PDF read; editorial tips are not code requirements.
- [Warrenwood Manor venue shopping workbook](https://warrenwoodmanor.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/Wedding-Venue-Shopping-Guide.pdf) — 15-page PDF read; comparison pages 12–14 visually inspected. Example terms are historical 2021 and Kentucky-specific.
- [Molto Bella venue comparison worksheet](https://www.moltobellaweddings.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/MB_Wedding_Planner_Venue_Comparison.pdf) — One-page PDF read; comparison structure, not California regulations.
- [One Story Weddings venue checklist](https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6373bbd7b8f87c3f80597d63/t/692f51c3a7d9fe3ff4687b97/1764708803836/The%2BOne%2BStory%2BWeddings%2BUltimate%2BVenue%2BChecklist.pdf) — Two-page Southern California checklist read; percentage heuristics not adopted.
- [Foothills coordination checklist](https://foothillsconferencecentre.com.au/checklist-for-coordinating-with-wedding-venues/) — Article and two-page PDF read; Australian operational process, not California law.
- [Event Fab producer site inspections](https://eventfab.com/pre-event-site-visits-checklist/) — Production checks reviewed; venue-specific engineering still required.
- [US DOJ accessibility guidance](https://www.ada.gov/resources/title-iii-primer/) — Official guidance reviewed; actual site accessibility requires assessment.
- [California ABC caterer permits](https://www.abc.ca.gov/licensing/license-forms/caterers-permit/) — Official current permit FAQ reviewed; each property and alcohol arrangement must be confirmed.
- [Ready.gov business emergency plans](https://www.ready.gov/business/emergency-plans) — Official public preparedness guidance reviewed.
- [A Savvy Event Napa/Bay Area planning team](https://asavvyevent.com/team/) — Practitioner description supports dedicated onsite production responsibilities, not a standardized workbook.
- [San Francisco entertainment permit guidance](https://www.sf.gov/get-place-entertainment-permit-your-business) — Official search-index text reviewed; direct page verification blocked. No parcel-specific legal conclusion.
- [Sonoma proposed special-event zoning update](https://sonoma-county.legistar.com/LegislationDetail.aspx?GUID=3795E6F1-7701-4414-AB81-C8BB81143BC1&ID=7768001) — Staff report reviewed. Agenda Ready status and missing final action mean proposed numbers must not be treated as adopted law.

Five freely accessible PDF workbooks/checklists were downloaded and read for this review. Original source PDFs remain research references and are not republished. Wedding Academy’s paid checklist description was discovered, but its full workbook was not purchased or reviewed. No universal restroom/security ratios, fixed hidden-fee percentage, attendance percentage or venue budget percentage were adopted from these resources. Requirements remain site- and event-specific.

## Venue age and operating history

Record construction year, wedding-operation opening date, current-operator start date and operating duration separately. For multiple structures, identify which building the year describes. Track conversions, rebuilding and interruptions. A historic lodge date does not prove the current reception building was built that year. Exact opening dates allow elapsed years; year-only records produce an approximate duration with an as-of date. Unknown stays Unknown — inquire.

## Value assessment



| Field | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| Parcel/APN, area, zoning, buildings | Confirm the exact asset; a venue address may cover multiple parcels or a leased portion |
| Owner versus operator | Determine what could actually be purchased or leased |
| Last recorded sale and date | Historical transaction, not today's market value; inspect whether it covered these assets |
| Current asking price and scope | Seller expectation; may include land, business, equipment or several properties |
| Assessed land/improvement value and tax year | Tax basis, kept separate from market value |
| Comparable closed sales | Match use, location, condition, acreage/building area and transferable approvals |
| Property estimate low/high | Only when comps or another documented method support the range |
| Business estimate low/high | Requires verified earnings/assets/contracts and valuation assumptions |
| Rent/lease term and assignment | For a tenant operation, land value is not automatically part of the business acquisition |
| Valuation date/method/confidence | Make the estimate reproducible and label evidence gaps |

California tax assessments and current market values can differ because of assessment rules. Do not use the assessed number as a purchase-price estimate. [California BOE explanation](https://www.boe.ca.gov/proptaxes/pdf/lta25023.pdf).
wiki.Venue value:
# Venue value assessment

Track **real estate**, **operating business**, and **lease/concession rights** separately. No defensible valuation range has yet been established for the two initial venue records. Unknowns remain explicit; not every venue is for sale.

## Can Zillow help?

Zillow says Zestimates apply to residential properties, excluding commercial property and vacant land. A residential estimate may inform the house component of an estate, but cannot value its wedding operation, event permissions, extra parcels or special-purpose structures. A Zestimate is not an appraisal. [Zillow FAQ](https://www.zillow.com/zestimate/).

## Evidence to collect for each venue

| Field | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| Parcel/APN, area, zoning, buildings | Confirm the exact asset; a venue address may cover multiple parcels or a leased portion |
| Owner versus operator | Determine what could actually be purchased or leased |
| Last recorded sale and date | Historical transaction, not today's market value; inspect whether it covered these assets |
| Current asking price and scope | Seller expectation; may include land, business, equipment or several properties |
| Assessed land/improvement value and tax year | Tax basis, kept separate from market value |
| Comparable closed sales | Match use, location, condition, acreage/building area and transferable approvals |
| Property estimate low/high | Only when comps or another documented method support the range |
| Business estimate low/high | Requires verified earnings/assets/contracts and valuation assumptions |
| Rent/lease term and assignment | For a tenant operation, land value is not automatically part of the business acquisition |
| Valuation date/method/confidence | Make the estimate reproducible and label evidence gaps |

California tax assessments and current market values can differ because of assessment rules. Do not use the assessed number as a purchase-price estimate. [California BOE explanation](https://www.boe.ca.gov/proptaxes/pdf/lta25023.pdf).

## How the research will work

Use assessor/recorder records for parcel and historical facts; [LoopNet's commercial valuation guidance](https://www.loopnet.com/cre-explained/tools/commercial-property-valuation/) and [Crexi commercial listings](https://www.crexi.com/) for relevant sale/lease evidence. Listings are asking prices; sold comps need actual closing dates and asset scope. Restricted or paywalled evidence is recorded as unavailable, not guessed.

Sales comparisons, an income approach and a replacement-cost approach answer different questions. A property's income valuation uses appropriate real-estate operating income and market-supported assumptions, not gross wedding revenue. Unique buildings may have weak comps. The operating business requires separate verification of earnings after normalizing owner labor, market rent, maintenance and one-time costs. A generic earnings multiple is not sufficient evidence for a competitor's valuation.

For an acquisition, model equipment, transferable contracts/approvals, customer deposits and obligations, lease rights, necessary improvements and working capital. Do not add a property value to an earnings-based business value if the same economic benefit is counted twice. Buying an established operation and buying its property are distinct transactions.

Public parks and government sites may offer rentals or concession/lease rights rather than a purchasable venue. Record Not applicable where ownership rules make an acquisition-value field irrelevant, with a reason; replacement cost is a different question.

This is an evidence-collection method. Preliminary ranges, when supported, remain research estimates with dates and assumptions; financing/purchase decisions need property-specific appraisal and business due diligence.

pricing_method: Keep package, venue-only and total costs separate. Derived venue cost per head is published venue fee divided by a user-selected guest count; it is not an all-in wedding quote. Null means unknown. Taxes, service fees, minimums and exclusions require written terms.
